issues.body: term_to_ntriples still appends TermRef.direction verbatim after `--`. TermRef is public and deserializable, so a caller can reconstruct or mutate a form with a direction containing SPARQL punctuation; to_sparql_update then incorporates that payload as executable syntax. The round-1 fail-closed requirement has not been implemented.
issues.fix_hint: Validate direction as exactly `ltr` or `rtl` before serialization, and validate the associated language tag. Make update construction reject invalid term metadata instead of emitting syntax, and add a test that supplies a malicious deserialized direction and proves no executable update is produced.
issues.title: Unvalidated base direction still permits SPARQL injection

issues.body: The test still uses assert_ne against exactly ["stale"]. Any other incorrect non-empty value passes, despite the documented default-build contract requiring an empty values vector. Because this test also runs with `computed` enabled, it still does not encode the distinct expectations for the two feature states.
issues.fix_hint: Under `#[cfg(not(feature = "computed"))]`, assert `computed.values.is_empty()`. Under `#[cfg(feature = "computed")]`, assert the exact expected computed value (`Bob`) and separately assert that `stale` is absent.
issues.title: Default-feature computed-field test remains vacuous

verdict.summary: Round 2 leaves both prior findings materially unchanged. The public, deserializable TermRef still allows an arbitrary direction string to be appended verbatim to SPARQL syntax, so a reconstructed form can inject update text. The default-feature computed-field test still proves only that the values are not exactly ["stale"], rather than proving the documented empty-vector invariant. The implementation therefore remains unsafe and its feature-state contract remains inadequately tested.
